data.raw_text:
NEWS UPDATE: Student journalist Jacob Baluyot has submitted a response letter through the Public Interest Law Center to the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group this Friday.

Baluyot received a subpoena on Tuesday from the CIDG over alleged involvement in the “violent incidents” during the Sept. 21 Aksyon Kontra-Korapsyon protest at Mendiola. In his letter, he clarified that he was present at the protest only as the safety officer of the Alyansa ng Kabataang Mamamahayag, alliance of publications of the Polytechnic University of the Philippines, and as a campus journalist covering the event.

Upon legal advice, Baluyot declined to participate in the investigation, emphasizing that being subpoenaed as an alleged leader treats him not as a witness but as a suspect.

The College Editors Guild of the Philippines denounced the subpoena, calling it an attack against the media, including student publications.

RELATED: https://t.co/7d68eVXgKO

Photos from the College Editors Guild of the Philippines
